one_line: Bengali novelist and colonial magistrate whose powerful yet contested nationalist writings shaped debates on nation, religion and power in late 19th‑century India.

appearance.age_look: Mid-40s, average height, slightly scholarly build with a straight posture that hints at both bureaucratic discipline and quiet intensity.
appearance.face: Oval face with a high forehead, medium-brown Bengali complexion, sharp nose, neatly trimmed black moustache, light under‑eye shadows from long nights of writing, and a calm, thoughtful default expression that easily hardens into firm resolve when challenged.
appearance.hair: Short, neatly combed black hair with a slight side part, kept close to the head, mostly hidden under a plain deep‑indigo Bengali turban (pagri) tied flat and low with a small knot at the back; a few discreet grey strands at the temples show with age.
appearance.costume: He wears a late‑19th‑century bhadralok ensemble: a long white cotton panjabi/kurta reaching just below the knees with subtle vertical weaving lines, over a slightly off‑white dhoti with narrow pleats and a well‑defined front fold, the dhoti border edged in a thin indigo stripe; over this he dons a tailored, dark‑navy woollen anglicised coat (frock‑coat style) that reaches mid‑thigh, with simple lapels, three dark buttons, and modestly padded shoulders, symbolising his colonial magistrate role; a soft, light‑cream shawl with a faint, fine red paisley border is sometimes draped over his left shoulder; on his feet are dark‑brown leather shoes in a simple Victorian style, slightly worn; he wears a small iron ring on his right hand, and a simple pocket‑watch chain in dull brass peeks from his coat.
appearance.signature: A well‑used, leather‑bound manuscript notebook tucked under his left arm with loose pages protruding, and a dark wooden dip‑pen with a metal nib held in his right hand, representing his dual life as novelist and colonial official whose words stir both devotion and debate.

ref_desc: A mid-40s Bengali man with medium-brown skin, oval face, short black hair under a deep-indigo turban, white kurta and off-white dhoti with indigo border under a dark-navy colonial coat, dark-brown shoes, carrying a leather-bound manuscript notebook and wooden dip-pen in a white, indigo and cream palette.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Bankim Chandra Chatterjee: a mid-40s Bengali man with medium-brown complexion, oval face, high forehead, sharp nose, neat black moustache and thoughtful eyes, his short black hair mostly covered by a plain deep-indigo Bengali turban tied flat and low; he wears a long white cotton kurta with subtle vertical weaving reaching just below the knees over an off-white dhoti pleated in front with a thin indigo border, and over this a tailored dark-navy woollen colonial-style frock coat to mid-thigh with simple lapels and three dark buttons, a light-cream shawl with a fine red paisley border draped over his left shoulder, and dark-brown Victorian leather shoes on his feet; include a small iron ring on his right hand and a dull brass pocket-watch chain visible from the coat; in his left arm he tucks a slightly worn leather-bound manuscript notebook with a few loose pages sticking out, and in his right hand he holds a dark wooden dip-pen with a metal nib, all rendered in a restrained palette of white, deep indigo, dark navy blue, light cream and dark brown, with clean lines and consistent details for use across many panels.
